rationale: The literature does not substantiate the claim that the specific craniofacial constellation of a prominent/broad forehead, high-arched eyebrows, bulbous nasal tip, and thin upper lip vermilion occurs in >80% of affected individuals across cohorts. While general craniofacial dysmorphism and developmental delay are widely reported across cohorts (e.g., 6/6 individuals in Feresin et al., 2025), comprehensive phenotypic evaluations highlight that clinical expressivity of individual features in Stankiewicz-Isidor syndrome is highly variable rather than uniform (Isidor et al., 2022), and specific feature breakdowns in available sources do not meet the >80% threshold across cohorts.

evidence.text: In a study of 24 additional unrelated patients with Stankiewicz-Isidor syndrome, the expressivity of most clinical features is described as highly variable rather than uniform across patients.

source.title: Stankiewicz-Isidor syndrome: expanding the clinical and molecular phenotype
source.quote: The expressivity of most clinical features in STISS is highly variable.

evidence.text: All 6 evaluated individuals from two unrelated families presented with developmental delay, intellectual disability, craniofacial, and skeletal anomalies, demonstrating complete penetrance for general craniofacial involvement but with notable inter- and intrafamilial clinical variability.

evidence.text: Clinical synopsis lists diverse and variable craniofacial features including broad forehead, broad uvula, cleft palate, dental crowding, and low-hanging columella without reporting an invariant or >80% penetrance for the hypothesized 4-feature dysmorphic facial gestalt.

conflicts: While general craniofacial dysmorphism is noted in 100% of some small cohorts (e.g., 6/6 in Feresin et al.), the specific combination of broad forehead, high-arched eyebrows, bulbous nasal tip, and thin upper lip vermilion lacks documented >80% frequency in published literature and conflicts with larger cohort findings emphasizing marked clinical variability.

new_directions.question_text: What is the exact per-feature frequency of standardized HPO craniofacial terms (e.g., HP:0000337, HP:0002553, HP:0000414, HP:0000219) across all aggregated published PSMD12 variant cases?
new_directions.rationale: Systematic HPO-based meta-analysis across all described cohorts is required to establish whether any single craniofacial sign or combination achieves high discriminatory value.

new_directions.question_text: Can automated computer-vision facial phenotyping differentiate Stankiewicz-Isidor syndrome from clinically overlapping proteasomopathies and neurodevelopmental syndromes?
new_directions.rationale: Given the reported variable expressivity of individual features, objective deep-gestalt modeling may identify subtle composite facial signatures where categorical criteria fail.
